newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Nov 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Nov 18.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- New Aspiration Party (NAP) narrowly beat the Democrats in the general election but NAP leader Chavalit Yongchaiyudh's chances of becoming prime minister depend heavily on the man he only recently betrayed, outgoing prime minister Banharn Silpa-archa. (THE NATION)

- New coalition must tread carefully. While NAP's General Chavalit may have the numbers to form a new coalition, academics and political analysts believe the government will be weak. They also believe the Bangkok election result clearly shows the country's middle class prefers a Chuan Leekpai-led government and Chavalit would have to tread carefully and make the right decisions if he is to gain their confidence. (BANGKOK POST)

- Election watchdog PollWatch said it had 5,512 complaints by the time the polls closed yesterday. The group's leader said it had succeeded in its goal to make the public aware of political abuses. The most common complaint by far involved vote-buying with cash. New Aspiration had 1,777 complaints and Chart Pattana was second with 799. (BANGKOK POST)

- Tycoon-turned-politician Thaksin Shinawatra quits as Palang Dharma leader. Thaskin resigned as leader of the party after it was humbled by the Democrats in Bangkok, its former political stronghold, where it managed to win only a single House seat. (THE NATION)

- Foreigners are extremely cautious in the wake of yesterday's vote. They don't expect a stock market crash, but want to see NAP's economic team before they make any moves. Foreign businessmen most fear and unstable NAP-led administration, and gridlock in Parliament. They are also ciynical about chances for a cleaner political system. (BANGKOK POST)

- New leader must act to rekindle investor confidence. There are three major issues that the new government must address as a matter of the highest priority: establishing a strategy with regard to the international investment community, addressing the important concerns that international investors have towards Thailand, and taking specific steps on policy issues. (BUSINESS DAY)
